predecessors.note: "conquered Songadh from the Mughals" (Baroda State page); the Gujarat Subah page has the Mughals still losing Baroda and Dabhoi in 1726. The state is a Peshwa-led confederacy member and sits inside the maratha-empire shape until 1802-1818.

successors.note: "Finally on 1 May 1949, Baroda State, the third largest state" merged into the Dominion of India; it became part of Bombay State and, on 1 May 1960, of Gujarat.

capitals.name: Baroda (Vadodara)
capitals.note: Songadh, the hill fort Pilaji took, was the headquarters "until 1866" on the page, which also has the Gaekwads conquer Baroda city in 1721 (Gaekwad dynasty page): the pages do not separate the two seats.

rulers.name: Pratap Singh Rao
rulers.note: The Gaekwad dynasty page has him "deposed 1951"; the Baroda State page has the reign to 1951.

correction.text: Baroda and the hill fort of Songadh in south Gujarat

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row. Pilaji Gaekwad takes Songadh in 1721; the Gaekwad page adds the city of Baroda in the same year, the Gujarat Subah page has Baroda and Dabhoi lost by the Mughals only in 1726. The extent of the early Gaekwad holdings is not described; a circle about Baroda and Songadh stands in (about 8,000 km2). Inside the Maratha Empire shape.

correction.text: the prants Kadi, Baroda, Navsari and Amreli, with Okhamandal

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The prants of Kadi, Navsari and Amreli, Okhamandal and Kodinar are drawn from 1802, the year of the Treaty of Cambay, because the page dates none of them (conf 1 events) and Kodinar is dated 1813. Area about 22,000 km2; the page says "In 1911, Baroda State spanned 3,239 km2" and "measuring over 1000 square miles", both far below the four prants and probably wrong (it would make the state smaller than one prant); no infobox area. The tracts are drawn as circles around the district towns.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the 1802 shape plus the parganah of Kodinar ("in 1813, the Barodan government acquired the parganah of Kodinar"). The 1940-43 Attachment Scheme (Pethapur from 1 February 1940) adds only villages.

region.text: Baroda and the hill fort of Songadh in south Gujarat

ledger.note: 1721: Pilaji Gaekwad conquers Songadh from the Mughals and the Baroda State is founded. "Thus the Baroda State was founded in 1721, when the Maratha general Pilaji Gaekwad conquered Songadh from the Mughals"; the Gaekwad dynasty page: "conquered the city from the Mughal Empire in 1721", held as a jagir from Shahu I. No month on either page.

region.text: the Kadi, Navsari and Amreli prants of the later state

ledger.note: 1802: bridging, page silent. The pages date no acquisition of these prants. The Treaty of Cambay of 15 March 1802 ("the British intervened to defend the Gaekwad Maharaja") recognised the Gaekwads' independence from the Maratha Confederacy against British suzerainty; the lands are drawn from that date. The Gaekwads had accepted the Peshwa's suzerainty in 1752 (Gaekwad page).

1808: bridging, page silent. "1808: a joint British-Barodan expedition approached Kathiawad and obtained bonds renouncing piracy from the chiefs of Okhamandal and other maritime states"; the page does not say Okhamandal was annexed in 1808, only that it is part of the later state.

ledger.counterpart: holder of Kodinar parganah (not named by the page)
ledger.note: 1813: Baroda acquires Kodinar. "In 1813, the Barodan government acquired the parganah of Kodinar."
1 February 1940: the Attachment Scheme begins with Pethapur and adds territory to Baroda until 1943. "1940-1943: Attachment Scheme added territory, starting with Pethapur on 1 February 1940."

region.text: the four prants Kadi, Baroda, Navsari and Amreli, with Okhamandal and Kodinar on the Kathiawar coast: several disjointed tracts

ledger.note: 1 May 1949: Baroda merges into the Dominion of India. "Finally on 1 May 1949, Baroda State, the third largest state" merged; an interim government had been inaugurated on 4 September 1948; it became part of Gujarat on 1 May 1960.

wars.name: Third Battle of Panipat
wars.outcome: Damaji Gaekwad fought in the Maratha army that was beaten at Panipat; no Gaekwad territory changed.
wars.note: The page gives no detail of Baroda's part.

wars.name: Second Anglo-Maratha War
wars.outcome: Baroda fought on the British side (listed among the British-side belligerents) and, per the Baroda State page, "acknowledged British suzerainty" after the war; its own borders did not move.
wars.note: The Treaty of Cambay of 15 March 1802 (Gaekwad page) had already placed the Gaekwads under British protection.

certainty.note: Revenue-collecting districts and tributes in Gujarat; the pages give towns and prants, not boundaries.

Four prants and the parganah of Kodinar are recorded administrative units; the tracts are scattered ("several disjointed tracts") and drawn as circles around their towns, so the drawn edge is approximate.

notes: Five pages opened (Baroda State, Gaekwad dynasty, Gujarat Subah, Second and Third Anglo-Maratha War). Pages that would not load: Damajirao Gaekwad and Maratha conquest of Gujarat (url_not_found). The pages do not date the acquisition of the Kadi, Navsari, Amreli and Okhamandal tracts; they are bridged at 1802 and 1808 at confidence 1. The Baroda State page gives 3,239 km2 for 1911, which cannot be right for a state of four prants (a gazetteer or census page should be opened to settle it). Cambay 1802 was the break with the Peshwa: maratha-empire (sa-05-d) could record the Gaekwads as a vassal 1752-1802 (Gaekwad page: "accept the Peshwa's suzerainty" in 1752); british-empire (sa-06) should record a vassal_start for baroda-state from 15 March 1802. Counterparts needing a dossier: Pethapur State (minor). The Baroda State page puts the merger into Bombay State in 1949 and Gujarat in 1960. Gazetteer lacks Kadi, Songadh, Amreli, Okhamandal, Kodinar, Pethapur as places.
